content.comment_body: I recently spent time sorting out the wiring for a [product_name] with an attached I/O module. There was an error in my wiring, and the system didn't work as intended. To troubleshoot, I created a test program: you choose which I/O (for example, 1 to 16) to display using ESC and the arrow keys. The display will show the I/O number, input state, and output state. If you set an input high, the appropriate output switches, also displayed on the screen. You can also manually turn outputs on or off by using ESC with the left/right keys. Be sure the system is in a safe state before testing. Using this, I quickly found that inputs 10 and 11 were swapped due to wiring labels falling off, which caused confusion. This method might be helpful for others in similar situations.

Hello, [product_name] provides a status view either directly on the unit with a display or if an operator device is connected. Navigate down until the clock is displayed, then left or right to view digital and analog inputs and outputs. For analog signals, press Enter to select a value and see a trend view, such as a temperature graph. Hope this assists.
Here is an example image of how an analog signal appears in the trend view on an operator device.
I knew how to check the inputs using the status screens of the [product_name], but I also needed a way to set outputs to ensure the output wiring was correct.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion highlights the need for a more interactive, efficient approach to testing I/O wiring with a [product_name] and expansion module. While built-in views allow users to monitor states, they lack straightforward methods for controlling outputs when verifying connections. One user overcame this limitation by developing a custom program, highlighting gaps in the official user experience for hands-on diagnostics.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the product to offer not just visualization of I/O status, but also a practical manual control feature for outputs to support wiring verification and troubleshooting.
